Study of 25 Wilms tumor survivors (nephrectomy) with long-term follow-up assessing cardiovascular effects including hypertension. Meets population (childhood cancer), intervention (nephrectomy), sample size (>20), and assesses late effects.

While the study includes patients receiving cisplatin/ifosfamide/carboplatin, the focus is on treatment response rather than systematic assessment of renal function at ≥1 year post-treatment. Renal dysfunction is mentioned as a secondary finding.

This is essentially a case series of 7 HUS cases following BMT. While it mentions renal complications, it does not systematically assess long-term renal function in childhood cancer survivors meeting the inclusion criteria.
This appears to be a review/commentary article rather than an original research study reporting on specific patient data. No clear sample size or systematic assessment described.

Prospective study of 74 children treated with ifosfamide, assessed 1 year after treatment completion. Systematically evaluates renal function including tubular markers. Meets all criteria: population (children <21), intervention (ifosfamide), sample size (74), timing (≥1 year post-treatment).

Large cohort study of childhood cancer survivors examining hypertension risk factors. Includes cisplatin and abdominal radiotherapy as exposures. While hypertension is the outcome, it is a marker of renal/cardiovascular late effects. Sample size adequate.
Study focuses on general late complications (hearing loss, hypothyroidism, ovarian failure) rather than renal function. Cisplatin exposure is noted but renal outcomes are not systematically assessed.

Study of 28 children with unilateral renal tumor undergoing nephrectomy/nephron-sparing surgery. Follow-up up to 100 months. Assesses renal function preservation. Meets criteria for nephrectomy intervention in childhood cancer.
This is a review/guide article for primary care physicians, not an original research study with patient data. No systematic assessment of renal function.
Study focuses on feasibility and efficacy of chemotherapy regimen. Toxicity was primarily hematologic. No systematic assessment of long-term renal function reported.

Retrospective study of 77 children with Wilms tumor. Long-term morbidity analyzed in 49 patients including arterial hypertension (2 cases). Follow-up extends over many years. Meets criteria for nephrectomy/radiation exposure in childhood cancer.
This is a review article discussing BMT-associated acute kidney injury. Not an original research study with systematic patient data on long-term renal function.
Review article summarizing toxicities of osteosarcoma therapy. Not an original research study with systematic patient data.
Comparative study of 30 Wilms tumor survivors and 17 individuals with unilateral renal agenesis. Assesses eGFR, tubular markers, and hypertension. Long-term follow-up. Meets all criteria.
Workshop proceedings document, not an original research study with patient data.
Methodological study deriving GFR estimation formula. Not focused on childhood cancer survivors or nephrotoxic treatment effects.
Study population consists of adults with von Hippel-Lindau disease and renal cell carcinoma, not childhood cancer survivors.

Study of 107 adult survivors of childhood cancer (treated 1947-1968, now >50 years old). Reports hypertension associated with nephrectomy during childhood. Long-term follow-up (decades). Meets criteria.
Methodological study on GFR estimation techniques. Not focused on childhood cancer survivors or nephrotoxic treatment effects.
Sample size too small (6 patients with bilateral WT). Study explicitly states only 6 patients were identified for analysis, which is below the 20-patient threshold.
Population-based study establishing normal BP values in healthy Turkish children. Not focused on childhood cancer survivors.

Longitudinal study of 165 childhood ALL survivors assessing obesity and hypertension. While corticosteroids are the main exposure, hypertension is a relevant renal/cardiovascular outcome. Sample size adequate, long-term follow-up.

Study focuses on survival outcomes with ifosfamide intensification. No systematic assessment of long-term renal function reported. Toxicity deaths and secondary leukemia mentioned but not renal outcomes.
Phase I dose-finding trial focusing on myelotoxicity. Small sample size (21 patients) and short follow-up. Not designed to assess long-term renal function.

Large cohort study of 500 adult childhood cancer survivors (median age 28, median follow-up 19 years). Assesses metabolic syndrome components including hypertension. Relevant for long-term cardiovascular/renal outcomes.
Study population consists of adults with seminoma, not childhood cancer survivors. Treatment with carboplatin/ifosfamide but wrong population.
Phase II trial focusing on pharmacokinetics and acute toxicity. Short follow-up period. Not designed to assess long-term renal function ≥1 year post-treatment.
Technical/methodological paper about reference material standardization. Not a clinical study on childhood cancer survivors.
Genetic association study focusing on cognitive impairment and toxicity prediction. While nephrotoxicity is mentioned as an outcome, the study does not systematically assess long-term renal function.
Treatment outcome study focusing on survival. States 'No organ failure or functional impairment occurred' but does not provide systematic long-term renal function assessment.
Study population consists of adults with renal cell carcinoma, not childhood cancer survivors.

Prospective study of 22 children treated with cisplatin, followed for mean 2.3 years post-treatment. Systematically assesses chronic nephrotoxicity including magnesium homeostasis and creatinine. Meets criteria despite borderline sample size.
Study of healthy aging subjects, not childhood cancer survivors. Population does not meet criteria.

Sample size of 21 patients is just above threshold, but study focuses on surgical margins and recurrence rather than systematic renal function assessment. Only mentions one patient developed renal failure.
Review article discussing pathological findings in nephrectomy specimens. Not an original research study with systematic patient data.

Cross-sectional and longitudinal study of 72 children with unilateral renal tumor, followed up to 5 decades post-nephrectomy. Systematically assesses eGFR decline over time. Excellent long-term follow-up data.
Methodological review comparing GFR estimation formulas. Not focused on childhood cancer survivors.
Study of adult CKD patients comparing diagnostic accuracy of markers. Not focused on childhood cancer survivors.
Methodological study about publication bias. Not related to childhood cancer or renal function.
Study of relapsed/refractory lymphoma in adults. Focuses on treatment response. Renal toxicity mentioned but not systematically assessed long-term.
Case report describing increased Tc-99m uptake after radiation therapy. Too few cases (mentions 3 patients total) and not systematic assessment.
Study focuses on caffeine monitoring and adverse effects. Sample size of 22 is borderline, but renal function not systematically assessed long-term.

Retrospective study investigating plasma creatinine evolution in long-term cisplatin therapy. Assesses influence of drug associations and comorbidities on renal function. Appears to have adequate sample size and long-term follow-up.

Prospective study of 23 pediatric patients with germ cell tumors treated with carboplatin. Median follow-up 58 months. Explicitly assesses nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity. Meets criteria for childhood cancer, carboplatin exposure, and long-term follow-up.
Methodological study optimizing GFR estimation equations. Not focused on childhood cancer survivors or nephrotoxic treatment effects.
Appears to be a case series describing renal atrophy after abdominal irradiation. Limited number of cases described. Not systematic assessment of large cohort.
Review article summarizing endocrine adverse effects of cancer treatment. Not an original research study with systematic patient data on renal function.

Retrospective study of 36 children with unilateral renal tumor comparing nephrectomy vs nephron-sparing surgery. Assesses eGFR changes over time into adolescence. Meets criteria for nephrectomy intervention.
Study focuses on survival outcomes with HIPEC. Mentions renal insufficiency as morbidity but does not systematically assess long-term renal function.
Review article summarizing ifosfamide use and toxicities. Not an original research study with systematic patient data.

Prospective longitudinal cohort study of 63 children treated with platinum agents (cisplatin/carboplatin), assessed at end of treatment, 1 year, and 10 years later. Systematically evaluates GFR, electrolytes, and nephrotoxicity scores. Excellent study design.

Study of 29 children treated with ifosfamide, median remission time 4.3 years. Assesses urinary NGAL, β2 microglobulin, cystatin C, and creatinine clearance. Systematically evaluates chronic renal failure. Meets criteria.

Study of 46 Wilms tumor patients assessing hypertension. While preoperative, it establishes baseline for understanding renal effects. However, this may be pre-treatment data. Need to verify if includes post-treatment follow-up.

Study of 20 children (11 rhabdomyosarcoma, 9 Ewing's sarcoma) receiving ifosfamide. Mean follow-up 16 months post-treatment. Detailed investigation of renal function showing tubular dysfunction. Meets minimum sample size exactly.

Study of 46 children treated with cisplatin for solid tumors, disease-free and off medication for at least 3 years. Compares renal function with controls. Systematically assesses permanent renal disturbances. Meets all criteria.
Review article on drug-induced hypophosphatemia. Not an original research study on childhood cancer survivors.

Cross-sectional study of 127 children successfully treated for various cancers including nephroblastoma (34 patients). Compares eGFR between groups. Assesses renal function post-treatment. Meets criteria.
Phase II trial focusing on tumor response and survival. Cisplatin used but renal function not systematically assessed as primary outcome.

Retrospective study of 37 children treated with ifosfamide, median follow-up 29 months. Identifies 6 children with glomerular dysfunction causally linked to ifosfamide. Systematically assesses renal function. Meets criteria.
Study focuses on growth parameters and body composition. While systolic blood pressure is mentioned, renal function is not systematically assessed.
Review article summarizing Wilms tumor treatment advances. Not an original research study with systematic patient data.

Large cohort study of 652 childhood cancer survivors diagnosed 1990-2000, followed to 2010. Reports significantly elevated incidence rate ratio for renal failure (IRR=13.4). Comprehensive long-term outcomes assessment.
Study of 26 Wilms tumor survivors with median follow-up 153 months (12.75 years). Reports one case of temporary low grade renal failure and transient hypertension. Long-term follow-up meets criteria.

Large multi-institutional study of 1,256 Wilms tumor survivors with 25-year follow-up. Comprehensive assessment of chronic health conditions. While renal-specific data may be limited, this is a major long-term outcomes study.

Review article summarizing late effects in adolescent cancer survivors. Not an original research study with systematic patient data.
